newsitem.title: USA: New U.S. tax law benefits IRA bullion investors.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. tax law benefits IRA bullion investors.

text.p: The U.S. balanced budget and tax cut legislation signed by President Clinton on Tuesday has an extra benefit for precious metals investors, according to analysts.
The law allows for a broader range of precious metal investment that can be purchased in personal pension plans with tax advantages, or Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs), analysts said.

On Tuesday Clinton signed the Taxpayer Relief Act 1997 which includes a provision (section 304) that broadens the precious metals investment options beyond the American Eagle gold and silver bullion coins to include gold, silver, platinum and palladium bullion coins issued by other governments including the Canadian, Mexican and Australian mints.
The new provision permits investment in other gold, silver, platinum and palladium bullion coins and bullion bars provided they meet certain fineness criteria.

"Although investors in individually directed retirment accounts may invest in a wide variety of precious metals mining stocks and mutual funds, they currently are unnecessarily restricted in their choice of physical precious metals investments," said Paul Bateman, executive director of the Washington DC-based Silver Institute.
Bullion is fabricated in several forms, among which the two most common are bars and coins.
With this legislation, Congress has in effect placed precious metals on a par with bonds and equities for the IRA investor, Bateman said.
The provision becomes effective from January 1, 1998.
Bullion coins provide the small investor with an economical way to make precious metals investments for diversification and portfolio protection purposes.

But while coins are convenient for smaller transactions, they do carry a higher premium than bullion bars, which may make them less attractive for investors choosing to invest larger amounts in precious metals.

To address that problem, the new provision also permits investment in gold, silver, platinum and palladium bullion bars which come in a variety of sizes ranging from a few grams to up to 1,000 ounces. Bullion products are among the most liquid of investments, with a 24 hour global market.

"Precious metals have uniquely been used for savings and investments since the dawn of civilization and millions of Americans invest in precious metals today," said Paul Bateman, executive director of the Silver Institute.
"They recognize that precious metals, such as silver, are an excellent way to diversify a portfolio and provide a hedge against inflation and financial uncertainty."
